run.question:
Something's broken — we're getting paged. Look at the app-265-prod-logs index
for the last 3 hours and tell me what's going on across our fleet.

report.summary: The paging evidence in app-265-prod-logs is a fleet-wide log index and the failures it records belong to cluster production-us-east-1, not to production-eu-west-2, which is the only cluster my Kubernetes access reaches. In the requested 3 hours (2026-11-23T14:46:56Z to 17:46:56Z) the index held exactly 7 documents, spanning 15:46:49Z to 17:16:49Z: 3 ERROR documents, all from production-us-east-1, and 4 INFO 'healthy' documents from production-eu-west-2 and production-ap-southeast-1. The us-east-1 errors form one chain: checkout-service reports 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 15:46:49Z, payment-service reports 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 16:46:49Z, and checkout-service reports 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 17:16:49Z. The deepest cause the evidence supports is repeated 30s timeouts on payment-service's upstream call to the payment provider stripe-us in production-us-east-1; whether that is a provider outage, a us-east-1 provider/config choice, or an enabled fault-injection flag there could not be determined, because I have no Kubernetes access to production-us-east-1 and Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every call. In the cluster I can inspect (production-eu-west-2) checkout and payment are demonstrably working: all 32 pods Running/Ready with 0 restarts, all deployments 1/1 available, payment logging 'Transaction complete.' through 17:46:31Z, and its flagd-config has paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable defaulted to 'off'. So impact in production-us-east-1 is established for checkout-service and payment-service only; no other service, and no other cluster, shows an error in this log evidence, and metrics/traces could not be checked at all.

claims.text: app-265-prod-logs is the only index in this Elasticsearch target and it held 7 documents total, so the 3-hour log view (2026-11-23T14:46:56Z–17:46:56Z) is the complete log content available: documents span 2026-11-23T15:46:49Z to 2026-11-23T17:16:49Z.

Of the 7 documents, 3 are level ERROR and all 3 carry cluster=production-us-east-1: checkout-service 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at 15:46:49Z, payment-service 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 16:46:49Z, and checkout-service 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' at 17:16:49Z.

The 4 INFO documents in the same window come from the other two clusters and report health, not errors: production-eu-west-2 checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 218ms', production-ap-southeast-1 checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.9%', production-eu-west-2 payment-service 'Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms', production-ap-southeast-1 payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' (timestamps 15:46:49Z and 17:16:49Z).

In production-eu-west-2 (the only cluster my Kubernetes access reaches) every pod is Running with all containers ready and restartCount 0, including checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm, and all 24 deployments report ready/available replicas equal to spec (checkout 1/1/1, payment 1/1/1).

payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (production-eu-west-2) logs successful charges during the incident window: 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' with distinct transactionIds, most recently at 2026-11-23T17:46:31.861714Z.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in production-eu-west-2 defines the fault-injection flags paymentFailure (variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), and both have defaultVariant 'off'; productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad, adManualGc and adHighCpu are likewise 'off'.

The observable checkout and payment deployments in production-eu-west-2 run images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout and 2.0.2-payment at deployment revision 1, with FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013 and PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080, and carry no provider-specific environment variable that would name stripe-us or adyen-eu.

The Prometheus ConfigMap in production-eu-west-2 contains an alerting rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh on service_name=checkout, span_name=~'.*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR over 5m above 0.5 for 2m with severity critical and cluster label opspilot-m1; the rule's expression and existence are visible, but whether it fired in this window could not be read.

The checkout and payment errors in production-us-east-1 propagate from payment-service's upstream call to the payment provider stripe-us: the 30s 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)' at checkout matches 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' in payment-service, and the later 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' is consistent with checkout shielding itself from the failing dependency. This is one observed log chain, not a verified provider outage.

Because the eu-west-2 payment-service reaches adyen-eu ('Adyen-eu responding normally, p95 180ms') while the failing us-east-1 payment-service reaches stripe-us, the us-east-1 failure may be caused by its region-specific provider configuration or an enabled payment fault flag (paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable) in production-us-east-1 rather than by the shared application image; no evidence from production-us-east-1 configuration was readable.

production-eu-west-2 shows no sign of this incident in its own evidence: checkout and payment pods are Ready with 0 restarts, all deployments are at full availability, payment logged 'Transaction complete.' up to 17:46:31Z, both flagd payment fault flags are 'off', and the eu-west-2/ ap-southeast-1 log documents report healthy latency and success rate.

Considered and rejected: that the fault sits in the accessible production-eu-west-2 cluster (for example a failing payment pod, crash/restart, or an enabled payment fault flag there). Every pod there is Running and Ready with 0 restarts and no terminated-last-state, payment completes transactions during the window, and flagd paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable are 'off'; the only ERROR documents belong to cluster production-us-east-1.

Investigate inside production-us-east-1 with cluster-scoped access: payment-service's connectivity and credentials for stripe-us /v1/charges, the us-east-1 flagd flag values for paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, and the payment/checkout deployment env for a region-specific provider setting; also confirm whether the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule is the alert that paged and when it started firing.

gaps: No Prometheus evidence was obtained: get_all_labels, get_metric_names, metrics_range_query (two windows) and list_prometheus_rules each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or kube-state metric series could be read and no baseline exists for any trend.

No Jaeger evidence was obtained: traces_list_services and traces_search for service 'payment' each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the sampled span view, parent-child edges and error-span counts for checkout/payment were unavailable.

My Kubernetes access covers only cluster production-eu-west-2; the failing cluster production-us-east-1 (where all 3 ERROR documents originate) could not be inspected, so its pods, containers' last termination reasons, events, flagd ConfigMap values, deployment env (e.g. stripe-us provider choice), services, endpoints and networkpolicies are unknown.

The Kubernetes events listing across all namespaces in production-eu-west-2 returned zero events in the authorized window (status no_data), so no event-based evidence of evictions, OOMKills, rollouts or probe failures is available for any cluster.

Error-focused log queries against production-eu-west-2 pods payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm and checkout-6578865d87-v6flf (filter err|error|fatal|fail|exception|panic|timeout|circuit, 2026-11-23T14:46:56Z–17:46:56Z) returned no matching lines; that is an empty query result, not proof the pods never logged an error.

Whether the stripe-us timeouts are caused by a third-party provider outage, a us-east-1 provider configuration error, or an enabled fault-injection flag in production-us-east-1 could not be determined; the declared fault itself was not observed and the time the setting changed is unknown.

Which alert actually paged is unverified: only the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule's definition in the eu-west-2 Prometheus ConfigMap was readable, with no rule state, firing history or start time (the change_history integration is not available).

Customer-facing impact beyond the three recorded checkout/payment error log lines in production-us-east-1 is unverified; the log index contains only 7 documents, so additional errors, other services, and the request volumes behind a 41% failure rate are unknown.
next_steps: Obtain read access to production-us-east-1 (pods, events, ConfigMaps, deployment env, Services/Endpoints/NetworkPolicies) and compare its flagd paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable values and payment provider configuration with production-eu-west-2's.
Check stripe-us provider status/latency and payment-service credential and connectivity configuration for /v1/charges in production-us-east-1.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger connectivity and then compare checkout PlaceOrder error ratio and payment span durations against a pre-incident baseline for both clusters before drawing any latency or error-rate trend.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
